declared.title: Early-career setback and future career impact
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « early-career setback and future career impact near miss » (2026-11-23)

population: junior scientists applying for NIH R01 grants (USA): proposals just below versus just above the funding threshold

findings.text: A near miss made scientists more likely to leave for good: more than a 10% chance of disappearing from the NIH system

support.sentence: On the one hand, it significantly increases attrition, predicting more than a 10% chance of disappearing permanently from the NIH system.

findings.text: Those who narrowly missed the grant and stayed later outperformed those who narrowly won it

support.sentence: Yet, despite an early setback, individuals with near misses systematically outperform those with narrow wins in the longer run.

findings.text: The authors argue the advantage is not only that the weaker left: the setback seems to cause an improvement in those who persevere

support.sentence: Moreover, this performance advantage seems to go beyond a screening mechanism, suggesting early-career setback appears to cause a performance improvement among those who persevere.

limits: a quasi-experiment around a funding cut-off, not random assignment
the gain is measured among those who stayed, while the setback pushed others out
one select group (US biomedical scientists); outcome = later publications and citations, not learning
